messages.text:
Great, now make a variation of the 8 ring layout where the outermost 4 rings are replaced by 2 quad-module rings.

For both, the 8 ring and the 4 + 4 ring come up with a local support, cooling and mounting design, explain your reasoning and recommendations - we will then use this new PR to love on.

I’ll develop the two layouts together in a new PR: the current eight single-module rings, and four inner single-module rings plus two outer quad-module rings. I’ll compare local support, cooling and mounting designs, keeping the existing service bounds and checking coverage and overlap for each option.

I’m treating “4 + 4” as four inner single-module rings plus two quad-module rings, which provide four outer chip rows. I’ll base the new PR on PR41 so its review shows only the new comparison and engineering design.

I’ll keep the service envelope fixed and compare the mixed layout with the eight-ring design on coverage, heat removal and assembly. The ACTS environment preflight flagged changed setup fingerprints, so I’m checking the installed runtime before using it for this revision.

The mixed layout will reduce the number of separate modules, but it still has eight radial chip rows. I’m keeping eight cooling tracks for the comparison and developing per-chip thermal pickups so each quad can remove four chips’ heat without relying on a single remote contact.

The first comparison is testing whether each thermal stem clears neighbouring modules below it. I’ve also included the pickup stack in the axial spacing; the earlier spacing cleared the module bodies but did not reserve room for that stack.

The central-stem proposal collides with lower neighbours on the dense inner ring and on the quad rings. I’m revising the pickup positions and retaining those failed clearances in the report. The overlapping bodies need carefully placed supports even when their sensor planes clear each other.

Using both faces of the sandwich clears the eight-ring stem collisions. The mixed design also needs a small inward adjustment to the quad contacts. I’m checking both arrangements across all discs, then comparing coverage, temperatures and service demand before making a recommendation.

The retained mixed layout has 102 singles and 50 quads—152 modules and 302 chips—and stays about 3.0 mm inside the plate radius. Both support screens pass across all 18 discs. The ACTS audit also agrees with the geometry calculation, while exposing more misses at inner transitions in the mixed layout. Its smaller uncovered area should therefore not be read as an acceptance qualification.

The report and drawings are ready. I recommend the mixed layout as the next prototype: it nearly halves module handling and improves cable demand, with a small increase in heat. Coverage gaps, warm thermal cases and service packing remain open.

I’m also using the OpenAI Docs skill to arrange the bounded usage-recovery follow-up after this turn closes.

[PR42](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/42) is open, stacked on PR41. It includes both designs, drawings, comparisons and the recommendation. Local checks pass; I’m waiting for hosted CI and finishing the session record.

The session record is now synchronized back to the original checkout and validates there. Once this turn closes, the recovery will import its final counters exactly once. Earlier turns will keep their existing attribution, and the recovery will make no scientific changes.

The final hosted build passed on PR42’s current commit. I recommend the mixed layout as the next prototype: it uses 152 modules instead of 296 and needs fewer mounting heights, while staying inside the service envelope. Both layouts still have coverage and service-packing limits to resolve before adoption.

I’m arranging the final token recovery for after this turn closes.

Created [PR42](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/42), based on PR41, with both layouts and their support designs.

The “4 + 4” variant has **four single-module rings plus two quad-module rings**—six physical rings providing eight chip rows. Both retain radial/tangential module axes.

![Disc layout comparison]([redacted]

| Per disc | Eight single rings | Mixed variant |
|---|---:|---:|
| Modules / chips | 296 / 296 | 152 / 302 |
| Maximum body/support radius | 182.337 mm | 185.503 mm |
| Margin to support boundary | 6.163 mm | 2.997 mm |
| Silicon overlap | 18.942% | 18.955% |
| Nominal heat | 796 W | 812 W |

For both, I propose:

- **Support:** a 6.3 mm carbon sandwich with modules staggered between its faces and per-chip graphite thermal pickups.
- **Cooling:** eight evaporator tracks forming 16 CO₂ circuits. Quads still require two cooling rows.
- **Mounting:** spring retention with a round datum and radial slot to accommodate expansion; three kinematic mounts connect each disc to the carrier.

I recommend the **mixed variant as the next prototype**: 49% fewer module installations, fewer mounting heights and lower reference cable demand, for approximately 2% more heat. Keep the eight-ring option as the modularity comparison.

The [report and drawings]([redacted] explain the reasoning and assumptions. Both remain draft designs: coverage holes, cable packing, warm-coolant performance and manufacturing tolerances need resolution. The mixed option also misses more of the sparse ACTS probes despite having less uncovered area.

Local checks, ACTS consistency checks and hosted CI passed. Session logs validate; final token recovery is scheduled once this turn closes.
